sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NanoBiT mini-Gαs recruitment assay performed with this FLAG-tagged construct; receptor-mediated signaling was detected, demonstrating both surface expression and functional coupling.
sites.rationale: GPR174 has no endogenous signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–18 as extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 19, leaving 18 extracellular residues between the prepend junction and the first TM helix (well above the ≥3-residue minimum). The exogenous HA signal peptide in the L1 construct is cleaved post-translationally, depositing the FLAG tag before M1 on the extracellular face; this is the only possible extracellular N-terminal junction. L3 (PMC13152116) independently confirms an N-terminal FLAG on the same receptor, though with an intervening BRIL domain, further corroborating extracellular accessibility at this terminus. Full-length GPR174 expressed in HEK293 cells with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed immediately by a FLAG tag (DYKDDDDA) at the N-terminus of the receptor, in pcDNA3.1; construct used for NanoBiT mini-Gαs recruitment signaling assays. GPR174 has no endogenous signal peptide (topology: EXTRACELLULAR 1–18), so after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG tag sits directly before residue M1 on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: All GPCR sequences used in this study were subcloned from the PRESTO-Tango GPCR Kit 54 into the pcDNA3.1 vector, with an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) signaling peptide (MKTIIALSYIFCLVFA) following by a FLAG tag (DYKDDDDA).

literature_notes: Five ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L3 both describe N-terminal FLAG tags on full-length, membrane-anchored GPR174; L1 is the primary citation because the FLAG is placed directly before residue 1 (no intervening domain), and the construct was used in functional signaling assays. L3 corroborates the extracellular N-terminal location but interposes a BRIL domain between FLAG and residue 1, so it is not a clean pin of the insert_after_residue=0 junction and is used only as corroboration. L2, L4, and L5 all describe C-terminal fusions (LgBiT or smBiT); the topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 296–333) firmly intracellular, so these are recorded in other_positions only. No ledger line supports any insertion in the extracellular loops (ECL1 78–88, ECL2 156–181, ECL3 256–268).

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminus of GPR174 (residue 333, topology INTRACELLULAR 296–333) fused to LgBiT–TEV–2×MBP in a full-length membrane-anchored construct used for complex purification; intracellular location confirmed by topology landmarks.
C-terminus fused to LgBiT–TEV–tandem MBP in the GPR174 structural/functional construct (PMC13152116); same intracellular junction as L2.
smBiT tag (VTGYRLFEEIL) added to the C-terminus of GPR174 with a flexible linker for NanoBiT mini-Gαs recruitment assay; C-terminus is intracellular (topology 296–333).
